Changelog

SCUBA 2.0.0 (development)

Split Seurat v5 layers on the Julia engine

  • With a SCUBA.jl that reads split layers (counts.<group> after split(), counts.1 / counts.2 after merge()), every accessor on such objects runs on the Julia engine: the logical layer names (counts, data) join the pieces, pseudobulk() aggregates them in one pass, and BPCells-backed pieces are read natively. An explicit piece (layer = "counts.1") returns every requested cell, NaN outside the piece, where the R engine drops those cells.
  • With an older SCUBA.jl (no split-layer support), Seurat objects with split layers use the R engine for every accessor. Previously every Julia-engine accessor failed on them, including fetch_data() with the default layer.

Unsupported classes are an error

  • Calling a SCUBA generic on an object it has no method for now raises an error instead of warning and returning the message text (so get_all_cells() no longer returns that sentence where cell names were expected). The message names the right function (fetch_data() used to report itself as fetch_metadata), the object’s class and every supported class (AnnDataR6, Seurat, SingleCellExperiment, scuba_source), read from the registered methods so it cannot drift. A Python AnnData object that the R anndata package did not wrap as AnnDataR6 (Python anndata >= 0.11 in a user-managed environment) gets a hint naming the Python stack SCUBA supports; other reticulate objects point to open_h5ad() / open_h5mu().

Fixes from the review of the 2.0 branch

  • fetch_matrix() on the R engine accepts keyed names ("rna_GAPDH", "AB_CD117-AB"), which select their assay as on the Julia engine; features from several assays are an error.
  • fetch_matrix() on Seurat v5 objects with split layers (counts.1, counts.2, … after split() or merge()) returns every cell, zero-filling features a layer does not hold, instead of the first layer only.
  • fetch_matrix(sparse = TRUE) converts other sparse classes, DelayedArray (HDF5-backed) and BPCells matrices to dgCMatrix without a dense copy.
  • pseudobulk() on split layers always runs on the R path (SCUBA.jl cannot yet index cells within a layer), and aggregates layers holding different feature sets.
  • pseudobulk() on an AnnData obsm modality requires layer = "X" instead of silently aggregating it under the default layer = "counts".
  • fetch_data() rejects conflicting layer and slot values on every engine and class, and keeps the very-wide-query warning on the Julia engine. A metadata column literally named obs_<name> on file-backed objects is no longer read as <name>.
  • SeuratObject 4 stays supported: fetch_data() passes slot = to its FetchData(), and Seurat objects use the R engine under SeuratObject 4.
  • The Julia engine no longer falls back to an embedded copy of its glue code for old SCUBA.jl versions (it did not match the R side); such versions are rejected, so "auto" uses the R engine. Paths and URLs reach Julia as values, so Windows paths in SCUBA_JL_PATH work.

Julia engine

  • SCUBA.jl is installed from its GitHub repository when the registry lookup fails (it is not registered yet); previously the engine was unavailable without a SCUBA_JL_PATH checkout. options(SCUBA.jl_url) / SCUBA_JL_URL override the source.

Python environment

  • reticulate-managed Python environments are pinned to anndata>=0.10.9,<0.11, pandas<3, scipy<1.15 and Python < 3.14 (py_require() in .onLoad). The anndata R package, now superseded, only wraps Python AnnData objects as AnnDataR6 for Python anndata < 0.11; later versions expose them as plain anndata.AnnData objects that SCUBA’s AnnData methods do not handle. This is an interim measure until AnnData support moves to anndataR (#173). Environments set through RETICULATE_PYTHON are not affected.
  • pseudobulk() and layer_names() accept unwrapped Python AnnData objects under both class names (anndata.AnnData, anndata._core.anndata.AnnData).
  • fetch_data(slot = ) on Seurat objects is an alias of layer; SeuratObject >= 5.4 no longer accepts slot in FetchData().

Pseudobulk aggregation

  • New pseudobulk(object, sample_by, group_by) sums (or averages) a counts layer over sample x group profiles for Seurat (including BPCells layers and split v5 layers), SingleCellExperiment (in memory or HDF5-backed), AnnData (in memory or backed, through reticulate) and file-backed .h5ad / .h5mu objects (open_h5ad() / open_h5mu()), returning the small features x profiles matrix and a table of the profiles. The full features x cells matrix is never materialised: the Julia engine streams every backend into a group accumulator, and the R engine uses the class’s own block-wise primitive (BPCells::pseudobulk_matrix(), DelayedArray::colsum(), a sparse indicator product). sample_by / group_by may be metadata column names or cell-named label vectors.
  • New pseudobulk_design() previews the same profiles from metadata alone (cells per sample x group, replicates per group, paired designs) without reading expression data.
  • New layer_names() lists the layers of an assay for every supported class.

Julia engine

  • SCUBA’s accessors (fetch_data(), fetch_metadata(), fetch_reduction(), fetch_cells(), get_all_cells(), meta_varnames(), all_keys(), features_in_assay(), reduction_dimnames(), default_layer(), default_reduction(), unique_values(), n_unique(), fetch_feature()) can now run on the Julia package SCUBA.jl, which implements the variable-resolution rules once for R, Python and Julia. The engine is chosen with options(SCUBA.engine = "auto" | "julia" | "r"); "auto" (the default) uses Julia when the JuliaCall package and a Julia installation are available and falls back to the legacy R implementation otherwise. See scuba_engine(), scuba_julia_available() and with_engine().
  • Seurat and SingleCellExperiment objects are read in place through RCall; BPCells layers are read natively from disk by SCUBA.jl. AnnData objects continue to use the reticulate path.
  • The Julia engine normalises behaviour that differed between object classes in 1.x: keys match only as key_, duplicates always collapse with a warning (including GAPDH + rna_GAPDH), partial misses produce one aggregated warning on every class, a single reduction dimension works on SingleCellExperiment objects, and unknown cells raise an error.

Breaking changes

  • FetchData() methods for SingleCellExperiment and AnnData objects (deprecated in 1.1.2) were removed; use fetch_data(). plot_dot(), plot_scatter(), plot_violin() and plot_ridge() now use fetch_data() internally.
  • default_slot() (deprecated in 0.10.0) now errors; use default_layer().
